what_its_for: Valproic acid is used to treat seizures (epilepsy), bipolar disorder (mood swings including mania), and to prevent migraine headaches. It works by calming overactive electrical signals in your brain.
how_to_take: Take valproic acid by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach. Swallow capsules and extended-release tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. If you are taking the liquid form, use the measuring spoon or syringe that comes with it, not a regular kitchen spoon. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause serious problems.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition, weight, and how your body responds. Most adults start at a low dose and the doctor slowly increases it. Take your doses at the same times each day to keep the medicine working steadily in your body. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store valproic acid at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine past the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking valproic acid, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness and may worsen side effects. Be careful driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking aspirin, especially in children, unless your doctor approves. Tell your doctor or pharmacist before starting any new medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements, as many drugs can interact with valproic acid.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting (signs of liver problems), unusual bleeding or bruising, dark or bloody urine, swelling of your face or limbs, confusion or unusual changes in behavior, thoughts of harming yourself, a significant increase in seizures, or signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face and throat. Also call your doctor if you feel more tired or weak than usual, or if your mood changes significantly.
when_it_works: For seizures and bipolar disorder, you may start to notice some improvement within a few days to 2 weeks, but it can take several weeks to feel the full benefit. For migraine prevention, it may take 4 to 6 weeks or longer before you see fewer headaches. Do not stop taking the medicine just because you feel better — continue taking it as directed by your doctor.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Valproic acid can cause serious birth defects including problems with the baby's brain and spine (neural tube defects) and can affect the baby's intelligence and development. It should not be used during pregnancy unless no other treatment works and your doctor has carefully discussed the risks with you. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control while taking this medicine. WOMEN OF CHILDBEARING AGE: Talk to your doctor about birth control options and folic acid supplementation. CHILDREN: Children under 2 years old have a much higher risk of serious liver damage. Use in young children requires very careful monitoring by a doctor. ELDERLY: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like drowsiness and dizziness, and may need lower doses. LIVER DISEASE: This medicine should generally not be used if you have significant liver disease. Your doctor will monitor your liver with blood tests regularly.
